key_insight: Q-DICE makes distributed quantum computing testable by compiling circuits to hardware-aware distributed QPU layouts and emulating realistic interconnect noise.
engineering_relevance: It gives researchers a practical way to benchmark distributed quantum algorithms and co-design hardware/software stacks before physical large-scale DQC platforms exist.
method: QPU slicing and stitching to build distributed backends and map circuits across QPUs
Physically motivated Kraus operators and stochastic channels to model nonlocal link noise
Boundary-aware transpilation that enforces distributed topology constraints
evidence_signal: The paper reports validation on multiple experimentally demonstrated circuits, including distributed Grover's search, with a worst-case fidelity deviation of 4% versus hardware results.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well the chosen noise models and topology assumptions match the target distributed hardware, so calibration quality is critical.
paper_title: Q-DICE: Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler and Emulator
